question: In recent days it has been reported that the Commission wants to introduce ‘extraordinary measures’ in areas of Kujawsko-Pomorskie, Łódzkie, Mazowieckie, Warmińsko-Mazurskie and Wielkopolskie provinces, where there is a high density of poultry farms. Poland is the largest producer of poultry meat in the EU and the world’s third largest producer after the US and Brazil, with an export value of EUR 4.4 billion!

Figures for 2024 show that production exceeded 3.5 million tonnes, of which more than 2.0 million tonnes was exported. This means that around 60% of Polish production is sold abroad, the majority of which (65%) goes to the EU market and around 35% to third country markets. 1.

The avian influenza virus (HPAI) is seasonal and its prevalence in Poland does not deviate from the EU average. As weather conditions improve in spring the virus naturally becomes less active. However, the Commission is proposing devastating restrictions just as the epidemiological situation is about to improve. Why is the Commission taking such radical action now?
Does the Commission envisage a ban on poultry exports from certain regions in Poland as part of the planned measures? If so, when will such a ban be introduced?
Will the potential embargo also apply to hatcheries, egg producers and other facilities?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.6.2025) The animal health measures (including regionalisation measures with movement restrictions) available to combat animal diseases relevant for Union intervention are laid down in Regulation (EU) 2016/4291 (Animal Health Law) and its delegated and implementing acts.

As the epidemiological situation of different diseases evolve continuously, harmonised measures are regularly discussed and decided at the Standing Committee of Plants, Animals Food and Feed2 (the Committee).

The Commission is aware that during the last months Poland has faced a specific deterioration in the epidemiological situation regarding highly pathogenic avian influenza in poultry, having difficulties in controlling the disease in certain areas with high density of poultry establishments.

As a consequence of that situation, the Polish competent authorities are implementing certain national measures in the zones of major concern. These measures were agreed with the Commission and presented at the Committee. These measures aim to contain the spread of the disease and operate within the framework of EU rules, according to the Animal Health Law.

The Commission then adopted Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/8963, amending the Annex to Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/24474, demarcating the areas listed as protection, surveillance and further restricted zone in view of the evolution of the disease situation. As stated above, the corresponding extent of restrictions is updated regularly according to the evolution of the epidemiological situation.
